title: Why Shaquille O’Neal Cards Are Suddenly the Hottest Ticket in The Hobby
summary: NBA Hall of Famer Shaquille O'Neal has had four championship rings for years. Now, the market is catching up to his clout.
body_markdown:
For years,[Shaq Fu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaq_Fu) was a punchline. The fighting game featuring NBA Hall of Famer[Shaquille O'Neal](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Shaquille%20O%27Neal&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) that debuted in 1994 was so bad that it became a cult classic, beloved for the same reason it was mocked. Yet two decades later in 2014, Shaq Fu’s sequel was crowdfunded, marking the Big Aristotle’s return to pixelated martial arts. Sometimes, all it takes is a little time.


Much like the career of[DJ Diesel](https://www.instagram.com/djdiesel/?hl=en) —Shaq’s EDM side quest—the market for Shaq cards was always a little puzzling. Here was a man that had done more commercials than seemingly anyone else, and had just about as much brand recognition as possible, all with an orange jacket from the Naismith to boot, and yet his rookie and insert cards lagged woefully behind (near) peers like[Michael Jordan](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Michael%20Jordan&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) and[Kobe Bryant](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Kobe%20Bryant&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) .


Before we go any further: *No, Shaq isn’t the GOAT* . However, being among the 10-best players to ever step onto a basketball court is nothing to scoff at, either.


While His Airness and The Black Mamba have owned the vintage basketball conversation for years—and the 2004 SP Signature Dual Auto Jordan and Kobe card (FMV: $140,000) currently offered in our[Sports Cosmic Pack](https://courtyard.io/vending-machine/sports-cosmic-pack) can get you both!—Shaq’s cards sat on the proverbial sidelines; a Hall of Famer with four rings and a level of mainstream fame that, in some ways, outstrips both the enigmatic guards, had prices that were, dare I say, affordable. Well, my friends, that gap is quickly closing.


# **The Numbers:**


[Across 86 of O'Neal's rookie-year cards tracked recently](https://www.si.com/collectibles/shaquille-o-neal-overdue-hobby-boom-gains-more-momentum) , more than half have *doubled* in value over the past three months, and 19 of them rose 200% or more.[When looking at his overall card market over the past three months, Card Ladder's Shaq index shows a 140% jump.](https://www.cardladder.com/players/Shaquille%20O'Neal) Needless to say, one of the NBA’s best big men is booming right now—and here are a few Shaq cards that showcase how quickly demand has risen:


- His flagship **1992 Upper Deck #1 rookie** , graded PSA 10, went for $2,600-$2800 as recently as March. It was going for $7,800 to $8,000 by the end of this August, a jump of 170% - 205%.
- A **1993 Ultra Scoring Kings** , graded PSA 9, went from $750 to $4,500+ in three months.
- Even a common, low-grade insert like the **1992 Ultra Rejectors** (PSA 8) went from $15 to $100 in 90 days.
- Need more proof? His **1995 SkyBox Premium Meltdown** insert climbed from $73 in early June to $763 by late August.


And here on Courtyard, a 1998 SkyBox Molten Metal Fusion pulled from[a basketball card pack](https://courtyard.io/vending-machine?category=basketball) carried a fair market value of $3,724, while a PSA 10 of Shaq’s 1992 Stadium Club Members Only sold on the marketplace for $1,495 in August.


Of course, with any vintage card, grading is a real factor here. From floods and fires to trash bins and garbage dumps, plenty of old cards are lost for one reason or another. Of those that remain, few score high grades, which can cause rising prices when demand spikes—especially when many collectors opt for[graded cards vs. raw](https://courtyard.io/blog/post/welcome-to-card-school-the-difference-between-slabbed-cards-and-their-raw-counterparts) to ensure that what they’re buying isn’t a knockoff.


# **Why Now?**


23 years after Jordan retired (for the second time), “[the 6-6 guard from North Carolina](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=276RCfR83bs) ” still reigns supreme. Even after[years of record-setting sales](https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/46673686/michael-jordan-card-sets-aftermarket-record-27m-sale) , Jordan’s Card Ladder index is up 42% since June, and continues to climb. At this point, many of his cards are simply more expensive than what most collectors are willing to spend. O’Neal offers similar nostalgia for a bygone era of NBA basketball, along with th same colorful ‘90s-era card designs, and the cultural cache of a fellow actor (lol). Until recently one of the few Jordan had that Shaq didn’t—outside of, well, a few rings—was the Hobby price tag, and we’re starting to see that moat erode, too, as collectors chasing their childhood drive the demand for a different former superstar.


The price of Shaq’s rookies and inserts also showcases a broader shift in how collectors are, well, collecting.


For years, The Hobby has yelled “buy singles, not packs!”, which is in line with the Courtyard experience of purchasing genuine, verified cards instead of a blaster at Target. In time, that’s led to some collectors choosing to consolidate from many chase cards down to a few grails, whittling their collections down to just a handful of absolute gems they’ll cherish forever. On the flip side, there are collectors that have grown tired of the never-ending chase for the next best thing, from[Victor Wembanyama](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Victor%20Wembanyama) to[Cooper Flagg](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Cooper%20Flagg) . Both are generational talents, and might end up in Springfield one day, but a player like Shaq is already there, and the logic goes that you can get top tier cards from proven winners for far less than a chance at a current start transcending greatness.


These mindsets have played a part in the vintage market’s rise, with many trying to scope out the player(s) from yesteryear that might be next to blow.


# **What’s Next?**


Whether it’s Jordan overload, 1990’s nostalgia, or collectors simply realizing a four-time champion with an ever-growing media presence had been undervalued for two decades, Shaq’s cards are no longer an afterthought for the hobby…which is why I’m going to start saving in order to buy this beauty of a card—[the 1996 SkyBox Z-Force #8 Big Men On Court](https://www.ebay.com/itm/257700055540?_skw=shaquille+o%27neal+insert&epid=3084905878&itmmeta=01M2R4A2MK90EF59DHR2FYCHC9&hash=item3c001ec9f4:g:j9IAAeSw61RqjI56&itmprp=enc%3AAQALAAABAGfYFPkwiKCW4ZNSs2u11xCFfdam5w2ZVmiGjkEKa7ZrkVFDxPdr71%2BJJYgy74jU7qIPEL5T280IfgT4CsOMP3lysgqIBsrK%2FIjyLDMGASM5rjkSyEM7I9MGc3qeLTPROtIIffE1TLxGdNAUomB1XK624NyTVpDIA8%2F4DAmdkV8jpDPjxDw6XY8Nmt%2F6eeYJFS7LvxAg3MvkE2TIq85tEnUaYivKytj62YIEEeZ5Nj2JSNqcWGmV%2FL9K1q%2B03X9ZCNRRaL0cb9QXJl%2FcG6mZ3olYkIkXW%2FZ7Mgovyt1N3%2FRB38upa9o2lQoYuKj2l0jIns5eT3Z2ZOkZ5nADmEzdafM%3D%7Ctkp%3ABk9SR4KsqISWaA) —one day.


Whether you’re looking to get in on the action via[our marketplace](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BrefinementList%5D%5Bmetadata.Category%5D%5B0%5D=Basketball) or[our basketball packs](https://courtyard.io/vending-machine?category=basketball) , we’ve got plenty of Shaq cards, along with those from his fellow teammates and leaguemates.
